newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA - HERMIS BANK SAYS STILL EYEING STATE BANKS.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA - HERMIS BANK SAYS STILL EYEING STATE BANKS.

text.p: Lithuania's Hermis Bank said on Tuesday that it was still eyeing the country's state banks but complained about a lack of reliable information concerning the state of their health.
"We have aims to participate in the privatisation of the Agricultural Bank and the State Commercial Bank," Dr. Nadiezhda Novickiene, the chairwoman of Hermis Bank's board, told Reuters.
"But we do not have enough information about either the banks themselves or the methods of privatisation to be used," she said.
Both banks have been slated for sell-off as part of the government's plan to hasten the pace of privatisation.
A number of local and foreign banks have expressed an interest in buying stakes in the state-run institutions, which have good branch networks.
But the State Commercial Bank has serious problems and some analysts have questioned its viability.
The bank recorded a huge loss of over 170 million litas in 1996 depsite a 165 million litas share capital injection from the government.
The Agriculture Bank had a profit of over 24 million litas last year but it admits it still has difficulties stemming from soft loans in the past to the country's ailing farming sector.
The country's other big state bank, the Savings Bank, is not slated for immediate privatisation.
